env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
mkdir $WORK/bin

# Imported closed unions: a LoGOs importer accepts only the concrete
# members named in the union, rejects a non-member even when it
# implements the union's method set, and rejects a non-member of a
# basic (method-less) union. The Go-facing projection of an exported
# value union is methods-only by design, so a Go client may still pass
# a non-member that implements the method set; that hole is asserted
# here on purpose and lives only in the Go module.
#
# The good module (w/impw) and the two negative modules (negm, negb)
# are separate modules so a bad fixture never blocks the good
# ejection. Rejection is checked at the compile boundary of the
# native build only: the ejected form is a methods-only interface,
# which Go cannot distinguish members from method-compatible
# non-members, so parity is asserted on the good module's run output.

cd w/impw
logos build ./...
logos build -o $WORK/bin/impw$GOEXE .
exec $WORK/bin/impw$GOEXE
stdout '^A:5/switch B$'
stdout '^B:s$'
stdout '^A:1$'
cp stdout $WORK/native.txt

cd ../goq
logos build -o $WORK/bin/goq$GOEXE .
exec $WORK/bin/goq$GOEXE
stdout '^N$'
stdout '^A:7$'
cd ../..

# Imported union rejects a concrete non-member that implements the
# method set.
cd negm
! logos build ./...
stderr 'cannot use'
cd ..

# Imported basic union rejects a concrete non-member value.
cd negb
! logos build ./...
stderr 'cannot use'
cd ..

# The good module ejects and the ejected output builds and runs with
# the upstream toolchain, byte-identical to the native run.
cd w/impw
logos eject -o $WORK/out
cd $WORK/out
exists $UPROOT1272/bin/go
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go build ./...
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go run .
cmp stdout $WORK/native.txt

-- w/impw/go.mod --
module example.com/impw

go 1.27

-- w/impw/lib/lib.lgo --
package lib

import "fmt"

type A struct {
	X int
}

func (a A) M() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("A:%d", a.X)
}

type B struct {
	Y string
}

func (b B) M() string {
	return "B:" + b.Y
}

// U is a closed value union exported to importers.
type U interface {
	A | B
	M() string
}

// Basic is a closed basic union with no method set.
type Basic interface {
	int | string
}

func Who(x U) string {
	return x.M()
}

func Pick(n int) U {
	if n == 0 {
		return A{X: 1}
	}
	return B{Y: "two"}
}

-- w/impw/use/use.lgo --
package use

import (
	"example.com/impw/lib"
)

// Describe switches over the imported union. The default branch keeps
// this fixture inside the assigned scope: membership checking of
// assignments, not switch exhaustiveness.
func Describe(x lib.U) string {
	return switch x.(type) {
	case lib.A => "switch A"
	case lib.B => "switch B"
	case nil => "switch nil"
	default => "unexpected"
	}
}

func Show() string {
	var u lib.U = lib.A{X: 5}
	return lib.Who(u) + "/" + Describe(lib.Pick(1))
}

-- w/impw/main.lgo --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/impw/lib"
	"example.com/impw/use"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(use.Show())
	fmt.Println(lib.Who(lib.B{Y: "s"}))
	fmt.Println(lib.Pick(0).M())
}

-- w/goq/go.mod --
module example.com/goq

go 1.27

require example.com/impw v0.0.0

replace example.com/impw => ../impw

-- w/goq/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/impw/lib"
)

// N implements the method set of lib.U without being a member. The
// Go-facing projection of an exported value union is methods-only by
// design, so this call compiles and runs; the LoGOs importer of the
// same union rejects the same assignment (see negm).
type N struct{}

func (n N) M() string { return "N" }

func main() {
	fmt.Println(lib.Who(N{}))
	fmt.Println(lib.Who(lib.A{X: 7}))
}

-- negm/go.mod --
module example.com/negm

go 1.27

require example.com/impw v0.0.0

replace example.com/impw => ../w/impw

-- negm/negm.lgo --
package negm

import (
	"example.com/impw/lib"
)

// C implements the method set of lib.U but is not a member. A LoGOs
// importer must reject the assignment at compile time.
type C struct {
	Z int
}

func (c C) M() string {
	return "C"
}

var _ lib.U = C{Z: 1}

-- negb/go.mod --
module example.com/negb

go 1.27

require example.com/impw v0.0.0

replace example.com/impw => ../w/impw

-- negb/negb.lgo --
package negb

import (
	"example.com/impw/lib"
)

// bool is not a member of the basic union int | string. A LoGOs
// importer must reject the assignment at compile time.
var _ lib.Basic = true
